Q1: Methylnaltrexone's hazard profile is largely data deficient across most categories, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity, environmental, inhalation, oral, dermal, and organ system hazards. The only exception is endocrine disruption, which has an expanded perspective of potential hazards (Tier 2).
Q2: Methylnaltrexone is not found on any lists of concern or low hazard. Given the numerous data-deficient hazard tiers, this absence likely reflects a lack of comprehensive study rather than confirmed safety.
Q3: While Methylnaltrexone has a moderate number of scientific literature references (537) and a well-defined molecular structure, its hazard characterization is notably incomplete. It lacks rigorous EPA evaluations (IRIS or PPRTV) and has no recorded toxicity values, resulting in most hazard categories being data deficient.
